findings.title: Lightness value changed unintentionally, not just converted to dark-light-choose
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The diff changes this to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the light-theme lightness value was changed from 30% to 70%, not just paired with a dark-theme fallback. This changes the light-theme appearance (lighter/dimmer text instead of darker), inconsistent with the stated goal of only adding dark-theme support.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved
findings.body: In the mobile `.topic-map h3` color rule, the original light-theme value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The converted rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which changes the light-theme lightness from 20% to 50%, altering the original light-theme color rather than only adding dark-theme support.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved
findings.body: The `.topic-map .map .number, i` rule originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` for both mobile files but was converted inconsistently: here it correctly keeps 20% but elsewhere (e.g., topic-post desktop map .number) the lightness was changed. Cross-check with desktop/topic-post.scss `.number, i` where lightness: 20% → still 20% but secondary 80%, in some other instances values were altered. This specific instance appears fine, but should be checked against similar occurrences for consistency since the PR introduces inconsistent treatment of the same selector/property across similar files.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved (group-member-info .name)
findings.body: The `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. After conversion it became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme lightness from 30% to 50%. This is an unintended visual change to the light theme beyond the PR's stated purpose of fixing dark theme support, and is inconsistent with the same selector in desktop/user.scss which also made this same change — indicating a systematic but unintended modification rather than a straightforward find-and-wrap conversion.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness value changed instead of preserved (group-member-info .name)
findings.body: Same issue as in mobile/user.scss: `.group-member-info .name` originally was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently changing the light-theme color value from 30% to 50% lightness instead of simply adding a dark-theme fallback.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30% in custom-message-length
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which changes the light-theme value from 70% to 30% lightness — a much darker color than before, not merely adding dark-mode support.
